entries.notes: First site in the coupled 92777 limit set. The renderer clamps or pads its dynamic vector to 32 records of size 0x144; the associated byte offset at 0x1516ECE and fill count at 0x1516F41 must be patched together.

entries.name: GroundItemLabelLayoutListLimit
entries.notes: Normalizes the synchronized ground-label layout list to 32 nodes. GroundItemLabelLimit validates and patches this comparison plus the coupled sites at 0x1519A4F, 0x1519AAA and 0x1519AF9.

entries.name: CLIENT_HandleUiPacket77
entries.notes: Registered at runtime as the handler for opcode 0x77 with an exact packet length of two bytes. The registration table is proven by the adjacent 0x9C and 0x9D handlers and its 24-byte-per-opcode stride. This entry tail-jumps to CLIENT_ApplyUiPacket77 at 0x1F0AB0. RemoteStash 0.1.0 calls it on the UI thread with the native packet {0x77,0x10}; this proves only the local client panel action, not an authoritative server bank session.

entries.name: CLIENT_ApplyUiPacket77
entries.notes: Consumes the action byte at packet+1. Action 0x10 follows the native open-stash UI branch and action 0x14 follows its separate UI branch. The exact 32-byte entry signature is pinned by RemoteStash 0.1.0 before the wrapper at 0x12DBC0 can be called.

entries.name: UI_ApplyInterfaceModeTransition
entries.notes: Observed x64 ABI (int32 mode, bool transitionFlag) -> void at a unique 20-byte entry signature. The state dispatcher at 0xC1E80 calls it as (2, true) from the unique callsite 0xC1F01 on the native stash-state 0x18 branch. RemoteStash 1.1.6 redirects only that callsite and, only inside a bounded hotkey-open scope, forwards (2, false). The exact behavioral meaning of transitionFlag remains gameplay-gated, so the semantic name and confidence remain provisional.

entries.name: CLIENT_ResetMouseButtonState
entries.notes: Zeroes six client input globals and returns. Their consumers at 0x8B989, 0x8BA1F, 0x8BB30 and 0x8B007 route held mouse-button actions into the local-player input dispatcher. UI_ApplyInterfaceLayoutMode at 0xB9C20 tail-jumps here for both the native stash-open layout transition and the state-1 inventory-close transition. RemoteStash 1.1.9 hooks the unique strict 32-byte entry and suppresses it only inside the thread-local hotkey-open scope, extended through the immediate companion-inventory close. The exact individual meaning of all six globals remains provisional.

entries.name: CLIENT_ResetMouseButtonStateWithFinalize
entries.notes: Reads the current local input-context index, zeroes the same six client mouse-input globals as CLIENT_ResetMouseButtonState 0x8D510, sets two additional state globals to 0x10, then tail-jumps to 0xF15C0 to finalize the indexed input context. Its strict first 32 bytes are unique in build 92777 and it has 16 direct xrefs. RemoteStash 1.1.11 preserves the native function and its finalizer, but snapshots and restores only the six shared mouse-input globals when this entry is reached inside the exact thread-local hotkey-open transition. The individual semantic names of the six globals and the complete role of 0xF15C0 remain provisional.

entries.name: UI_CloseActiveInterfaceStates
entries.notes: Builds a temporary list of active UI-state identifiers and closes each entry through UI_CloseInterfaceState at 0xC84C6. Runtime capture during a click-to-move action proves the call chain 0x102590 -> 0xC8240 -> 0xC84C6. The observed x64 arguments are two integer or boolean mode values, but their complete semantic meaning remains provisional.

entries.name: WorldActionCloseActiveInterfacesCall
entries.notes: Exact E8 AB 5C FC FF call to UI_CloseActiveInterfaceStates. A RemoteStash 1.1.7 runtime stack capture proved this callsite as the close cascade reached when clicking the world to move while both remote stash state 0x18 and inventory state 1 are open. RemoteStash redirects only this callsite and uses a thread-local scope so only the movement-driven inventory close is suppressed; explicit inventory hotkey and close-button paths remain native.

entries.name: UI_OpenInterfaceState
entries.notes: Opens or refreshes a native UI state with observed x64 ABI (int32 state, bool secondary) -> bool. The entry indexes the UI-state byte array with the signed state argument, validates the transition, and dispatches the state-specific UI message. Its strict 68-byte prologue is unique in build 92777. Direct callers pass state 1 for inventory, while CLIENT_ApplyUiPacket77 opens the stash with state 0x18. RemoteStash 1.1.3 proved that suppressing state 1 before native composition leaves a broken desktop shell. RemoteStash 1.1.5 instead delegates every open first; after a successful remote state 0x18 open, a bounded one-shot hotkey ticket may close the companion state 1 through UI_CloseInterfaceState. No native open is suppressed.

entries.name: UI_PlayerInventory_RefreshGoldControls
entries.notes: PlayerInventoryPanel refresh method with ABI (panel) -> void. It resolves gold_amount and gold_button through UI_FindChildWidgetByName, refreshes the displayed bank-gold value and applies the native gold-button state. RemoteStash 0.1.0 hooks its strict 32-byte prologue, calls the original first, then measures the active panel, grid, footer and private button for fail-closed dynamic placement.

entries.name: UI_ButtonWidget_OnClick
entries.notes: Generic ButtonWidget click handler with probable ABI (button, inputMessage) -> void. Runtime type metadata proves onClickMessage at button+0x558; the handler dispatches that embedded message at 0x8F1069. RemoteStash 0.1.0 hooks the strict 32-byte prologue and consumes only hash 0x055A7CEA95897DC9 for PlayerInventoryPanelMessage:RemoteStash, forwarding every other button unchanged.

entries.name: ITEMS_GetDimensions
entries.notes: Returns an item's one-byte width and height through the proven x64 ABI (item, widthOut, heightOut, sourceFile, sourceLine) -> void. INVENTORY_FindFreePosition calls it before choosing a scan direction; CubeQuickMove pins its 32-byte prologue and uses it only after the vanilla Cube search succeeds.

entries.name: D2GAME_ServerPacketCallbackTable
entries.notes: Base of the authoritative 256-entry server packet callback table, with one eight-byte function pointer per opcode. Runtime captures prove slots 0x01-0x12 point respectively to 0x4AC050, 0x4ACE20, 0x4ACE40, 0x4ACE60, 0x4ACE80, 0x4ACF80, 0x4AD030, 0x4AD0E0, 0x4AD100, 0x4AD120, 0x4AD140, 0x4AD230, 0x4AD330, 0x4AD3E0, 0x4AD490, 0x4AD4B0, 0x4AD4D0 and 0x4AD4F0 on build 92777. PotionAutoPickup 1.1.1 validates every pointer before redirecting those player-action slots; slot 0x16 remains the vanilla pickup callback at 0x4B9DF0.

entries.name: INVENTORY_GetFreeBeltSlot
entries.notes: Chooses a free belt cell with proven x64 ABI (inventory, item, freeSlotOut, allowAnyBeltable) -> int32. The automatic ground-pickup helper calls it at 0x471C31. Its strict 32-byte prologue is unique in build 92777. PotionAutoPickup 1.1.1 hooks it only inside a thread-local scope bound to the exact inventory and ground item selected by the plugin.

entries.name: InventoryPlayerHeightPlacementGate
entries.notes: The exact bytes 40 80 FE 01 compare the item height with one inside INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. Equality calls the bottom-right weighted search at 0x38D8F0; other heights continue into the player top-left path. CubeQuickMove does not patch this shared branch.

entries.name: INVENTORY_ResolveOccupancyGrid
entries.notes: Resolves the temporary occupancy grid used by free-position searches with ABI (inventory, gridIndex, gridInfo) -> occupancyGrid. The Cube caller supplies native page 3, so INVENTORY_FindFreePosition passes grid index 5. INVENTORY_GetFreeBeltSlot passes grid index 1 with the static belt grid info at 0x237B638; the resulting grid exposes width at +0x10, height at +0x11 and the cell item-pointer array at +0x18.

entries.name: INVENTORY_SearchBottomRightWeighted
entries.notes: Native bottom-right-to-top-left weighted placement search with ABI (inventory, occupancyGrid, freeXOut, freeYOut, widthByte, heightByte) -> int32. Its only vanilla xref is the height-equals-one branch at 0x386754. CubeQuickMove 0.1.0 reused it for taller Cube items, but that design was retired after the first gameplay witness failed; 0.1.1 scans the resolved occupancy grid directly.

entries.name: INVENTORY_BuildGridContext
entries.notes: Builds the temporary grid context consumed by INVENTORY_ResolveOccupancyGrid with ABI (itemDataContextByte, inventoryRecordId, reservedZero, gridContextOut) -> void. The exact call sequence is proven inside INVENTORY_FindFreePosition.

entries.name: CubeAutomaticFindFreePositionCall_0FA33D
entries.notes: Automatic placement call E8 6E C2 28 00 to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. Its caller writes the sixth page argument as native Cube page 3 with C6 44 24 28 03. CubeQuickMove 0.1.2 owned this five-byte call; 0.1.3 retains it in the 27-site page-3-capable set.

entries.name: CubeAutomaticFindFreePositionCall_2C7306
entries.notes: Automatic placement call E8 A5 F2 0B 00 to INVENTORY_FindFreePosition. Its caller writes the sixth page argument as native Cube page 3 with C6 44 24 28 03. CubeQuickMove 0.1.2 owned this five-byte call; 0.1.3 retains it in the 27-site page-3-capable set.

entries.name: CubeAutomaticFindFreePositionCall_471D62

It returns zero without mutation when carried gold plus personal bank gold is insufficient; otherwise it debits carried gold first, then only the required remainder from the personal bank, and returns one. It reads stat ids 14 and 15, never the shared stash. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777 and D2GAME_NPC_RepairHandler calls it at 0x53FF7B.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_Rcv0x39_ResetStatsAndSkillsWithNpc
entries.notes: Authoritative server callback with observed ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32. A controlled 92777 runtime read proved slot 0x39 of the server callback table at D2R+0x1D2A790 points here. It requires exactly five bytes, decodes the NPC GUID at +1, validates the interaction and NPC service record, and for Akara requires current-difficulty quest 0x29 RewardPending before calling D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetStatsAndSkills at 0x4B2A23. Native first-use bookkeeping follows through QUESTS_ConsumeAkaraRespecReward.

entries.name: D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetStatsAndSkills
entries.notes: Native combined respec transaction with observed ABI (game, player) -> int32. Its only direct caller is the authoritative opcode 0x39 callback at 0x4B2A23. It resets and refunds invested skills through D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetSkills, resets base Strength/Energy/Dexterity/Vitality through D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetBaseStats, refreshes inventory and derived state, attaches the native sound, and returns one.

entries.name: D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetSkills
entries.notes: Iterates the player's class skill list, reads each invested base level, removes the skill ranks through the native reset/update path, sums the refunded ranks, and adds that total to stat id 5 (unspent skill points). D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetStatsAndSkills calls it first at 0x580F30.

entries.name: D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetBaseStats
entries.notes: Resets player base stat ids 0 through 3 to the class starting Strength, Energy, Dexterity and Vitality values, refunds the removed points into stat id 4, and routes the dependent life, mana and stamina recalculations through native helpers. D2GAME_PLAYER_ResetStatsAndSkills calls it at 0x580F3B.

entries.name: QUESTS_ConsumeAkaraRespecReward
entries.notes: Performs native post-respec bookkeeping for current-difficulty quest 0x29 with observed ABI (game, player) -> void. It sets RewardGranted, clears RewardPending and then evaluates an additional quest flag before the remaining quest-event path. The opcode 0x39 callback is its only direct caller and invokes it only when the NPC service record carries a nonzero quest field. Paid repeats must bypass this routine to preserve quest flags bit-exactly.

The non-null path returns dword [unit+0x00]; AITACTICS_SetVelocity calls it twice before resolving monster AI parameters. RogueScoutMovement uses it only after a non-null guard and requires its strict build-92777 prologue.

entries.name: D2GAME_MONSTERMODE_SetVelocityParams
entries.notes: Observed ABI (aiParam, pathType, velocityPercent, distance) -> void. It writes nonzero path type at aiParam+0x20, nonzero velocity percent at +0x24 and a clamped nonzero distance byte at +0x28. A zero velocity argument is a sentinel that normally preserves the previous field; RogueScoutMovement clears +0x24 explicitly only inside a thread-local, aiParam-matched Act I Rogue follow scope so an absolute configured velocity of 11 remains the exact BKVince baseline.

entries.name: D2GAME_PETAI_PetMove
entries.notes: Authoritative pet movement helper with observed x64 ABI (game, owner, unit, motionType, run, velocityPercent, steps) -> int32. The 49-byte wildcard signature is unique in build 92777 and its four direct callers are 0x5BEC72, 0x5BECA1, 0x5BEFCD and 0x5BF00A. D2MOO provides semantic ancestry: Hireable uses motion 0 for near following and motion 1 for catch-up, while later motion values cover wander, warp and spacing. It reads stat 80 from the player or monster and adds the minion owner's value, preserves a separate MF<=-100 gate, applies diminishing returns to unique/set/rare, leaves magic linear, then applies ItemRatio minima, Treasure Class modifiers and native RNG. Its strict 38-byte prologue is unique in build 92777.

entries.name: HDItemsJsonCodePaddingBlock
entries.notes: Unique 26-byte code-padding block inside HDItems_LoadBaseItemAssetsJson. Vanilla reads key byte 2, pads it when absent, then unconditionally stores ASCII space as byte 3 (0F B6 46 02 84 C0 75 09 66 C7 44 24 26 20 20 EB 09 88 44 24 26 C6 44 24 27 20). The Four Character Item Codes memory patch replaces the block in place with two symmetric byte reads and NUL-to-space fallbacks. entries.name: D2GAME_SHAREDSTASH_DepositHandler
entries.notes: Native shared-stash deposit handler. It resolves an auxiliary UNIT_PLAYER from the packet GUID, requires state 0xBA through STATES_CheckState, validates that auxiliary inventory's owner GUID against the requesting player, and confirms the proxy in the player's corpse registry. RemoteStash owns the inline hook; MassID does not hook this function.

entries.name: D2GAME_SHAREDSTASH_WithdrawalHandler
entries.notes: Native shared-stash withdrawal handler with the same auxiliary UNIT_PLAYER, state 0xBA, inventory-owner and corpse-registry validation chain as the deposit path. Its ITEMS_PlaceItemForPlayer call uses the auxiliary unit as the shared inventory holder. RemoteStash owns the inline hook; MassID only reuses the proven accessors.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_Rcv0x34_IdentifyItemsWithNpc
entries.notes: Authoritative server callback in dispatch-table slot 0x34 with ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32. It requires exactly 0x15 bytes and is stored at 0x1D2A930, which maps to opcode 0x34 from the table base 0x1D2A790. MassID 0.2.4 recognizes two private payload markers before this vanilla path and delegates every normal Cain request unchanged.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_ExecuteEvents
entries.notes: Confirmed-static authoritative damage/event commit with logical bounds 0x44CE80..0x44D569 and ABI (game, attacker, defender, bMissile, D2Damage*) -> void. Its 31-byte entry signature is unique and it has 36 direct callers. Melee callsite 0x44B3FA passes bMissile=0 while missile callsite 0x436F95 passes 1, so this is a shared commit surface rather than an exclusively-melee hit seam.

entries.name: D2GAME_EventFunc14_ItemFreeze
entries.notes: Confirmed-static EventFunc14 ItemFreeze callback. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in build 92777; zero direct xrefs are expected because the native dispatcher calls handlers indirectly. The D2R callback frame transports nine positions, not a seven-argument ABI copied from legacy D2MOO.

entries.name: D2GAME_EventFunc20_SkillOnAttackHitKill
entries.notes: Confirmed-static EventFunc20 callback for skill-on-attack/hit/kill nodes. Its strict 33-byte entry signature is unique; packed node payload uses high-word stat id and low-word layer before the layered stat getter. Dispatch is indirect with a nine-position D2R frame, so zero direct xrefs do not imply an unused handler.

entries.name: SUNIT_CanDamageTarget
entries.notes: Confirmed-static server target-permission predicate with logical bounds 0x48E060..0x48E248 and ABI (game, attacker, candidate) -> int32. Its 19-byte entry signature is unique; direct callers 0x44CEC1 and 0x44A9C9 prove its role before damage commit and finalization. It resolves owners/minions, town, rooms and hostile relation but does not prove distance or LOS.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_FillDamageValues
entries.notes: Confirmed-static native damage builder with bounds 0x44C030..0x44CDC8 and ABI (game, attacker, defender, D2Damage*, mode, SrcDam) -> void. Its unique 30-byte signature and eight callers are governed. The mode-zero path resolves weapon-mastery Critical, passive Critical Strike, then Deadly Strike with short-circuiting; success doubles physical and sets the shared result bit 0x2000.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_ApplyDamageBonuses
entries.notes: Confirmed-static eight-argument native damage-bonus helper with bounds 0x44D710..0x44D9E5 and ABI (attacker, getStats, item, minDamage, maxDamage, enhancedPct, flatDamage, SrcDam) -> int32. Its 31-byte signature is unique with six callers and nine material callees. This proof establishes the generic helper only; it does not validate the prototype's historical Smite composition.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_ApplyMonsterCritical
entries.notes: Confirmed-static monster-critical stage with bounds 0x5889E0..0x588AF4, unique 32-byte signature and ABI (attacker, defender, D2Damage*) -> void. It rolls the attacker seed against MonStats chance and doubles six damage components. It does not set the player Critical/Deadly result bit 0x2000 and is therefore a distinct result path.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_CalculateTotalDamage
entries.notes: Confirmed-static component-aware damage resolver with bounds 0x44DF10..0x44ECE0 and ABI (game, attacker, defender, D2Damage*) -> void. Its 49-byte signature is unique with four callers. It applies resistances, reductions, absorb and final totals and delegates to the governed resistance resolver 0x4523E0.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_FinalizeDamage
entries.notes: Confirmed-static final damage/status/mode/death stage with bounds 0x44A9B0..0x44B2A2, unique 30-byte signature and ABI (game, attacker, defender, D2Damage*) -> void. It has 32 direct callers and follows ExecuteEvents on the governed melee and missile chains. Runtime ordering of reactions, death and packets remains a MEC-01 witness.

entries.name: D2Damage_CopyConstructor
entries.notes: Confirmed-static deep-copy constructor with bounds 0x4494B0..0x4496DF, unique 32-byte signature and ABI (destination, source) -> destination for the build-92777 0x180-byte D2Damage object. It copies scalars, reconstructs the internal SBO container and constructs the owned subobject at +0x158.

entries.name: D2Damage_Destructor
entries.notes: Confirmed-static destructor with bounds 0x4496E0..0x449752, unique 32-byte signature and ABI (D2Damage*) -> void for the 0x180-byte record. It destroys the owned subobject at +0x158 and releases the +0x40 container only when it is outside the inline SBO storage.

entries.name: D2GAME_EventFunc15_OpenWounds
entries.notes: Confirmed-static Open Wounds event callback with bounds 0x584170..0x584316 and unique 24-byte signature. The native nine-position callback frame supplies game, event, attacker, target and packed layered-stat payload. It rolls the attacker seed, computes the native OW value and delegates state 62 to the generic curse/statlist helper; the exact BSS tuple for duration/stat id still requires a runtime read-only witness.

entries.name: D2GAME_EventFunc16_CrushingBlow
entries.notes: Confirmed-static Crushing Blow event callback with bounds 0x583150..0x583276 and unique 32-byte signature. It consumes the D2Damage pointer and packed chance from the native nine-position callback frame, rolls the attacker seed, builds the target-class divisor context and calls the native Crushing Blow core at 0x581BD0.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_ApplyLifeAndManaLeech
entries.notes: Confirmed-static unique life/mana leech consumer with bounds 0x450C90..0x451380, unique 32-byte signature and ABI (game, attacker, defender, D2Damage*) -> void. Its only direct caller is ExecuteEvents at 0x44D038. It consumes raw percentages at D2Damage+0x120/+0x124, applies Drain and difficulty divisors, and rewrites those fields with native-adjusted percentages. It then derives and caps the separately credited life/mana amounts; the rewritten fields are not direct witnesses of the credited amounts.

entries.name: D2GAME_DispatchUnitStatEventList
entries.notes: Confirmed-static native unit-stat event-list dispatcher with bounds 0x5881E0..0x58844B and unique 16-byte signature. Eight direct callers include the damage-event wrapper at 0x44D5F2. It walks attacker+0xE0, invokes node callbacks through a nine-position D2R frame and safely performs deferred deletion after callback return.

entries.name: D2GAME_ApplyCrushingBlowCore
entries.notes: Confirmed-static Crushing Blow core with bounds 0x581BD0..0x581EC7, unique 24-byte signature and ABI (game, attacker, target, context) -> int32. Its two callers are 0x51D950 and EventFunc16 at 0x583257. It selects target divisors, applies player-count and physical resistance, writes HP, sets D2Damage result bit 2 on lethal damage and applies overlay 147 when positive.

entries.name: D2GAME_ApplyCurseStateStatList
entries.notes: Confirmed-static generic curse/state statlist applicator with bounds 0x433D20..0x4341DC, unique 24-byte signature and 32 callers including Open Wounds. It validates state/target, refreshes matching lists, rejects weaker replacements, unlinks mismatches, allocates and posts new lists, schedules expiration event 12 and installs a remove callback. It is generic and must not be named as an Open-Wounds-only primitive.

entries.name: D2GAME_DefaultCurseStateRemoveCallback
entries.notes: Confirmed-static default curse/state removal callback with bounds 0x436240..0x4362DC and unique 24-byte signature. It unregisters the pending event, preserves dead/stay-death handling, disables the state and refreshes animation, passives and player state as required. It is shared by generic state lists and is not Open-Wounds-exclusive.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_PrepareAndQueueCombatRecord
entries.notes: Confirmed-static combat-record preparation wrapper with logical bounds 0x44B600..0x44B71B, a unique 33-byte signature, 31 direct callers and ABI (game, attacker, defender, D2Damage*, SrcDam:uint8) -> void. It conditionally runs FillDamageValues, runs CalculateTotalDamage, derives WILLDIE and calls the unique combat-node linker at 0x44B703. It prepares target-specific state and is not a safe secondary-damage primitive.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_AllocateAndLinkCombatRecord
entries.notes: Confirmed-static combat-node allocator/linker with logical bounds 0x4507B0..0x4509A3, unique 32-byte signature and ABI (game, attacker, defender, const D2Damage*) -> void. Its only direct caller is 0x44B703. It allocates 0x1A0 bytes, records attacker/defender type and GUID, deep-copies D2Damage to node+0x18 and links the node under attacker+0x108; it applies no HP or reactions.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_ConsumeMeleeCombatRecord
entries.notes: Confirmed-static stored-melee-combat consumer with logical bounds 0x44B2B0..0x44B5F5, unique 34-byte signature, 36 direct callers and ABI (game, attacker, defender, rangeBonus) -> bool/uint8. It finds the node by type/GUID, deep-copies its D2Damage, validates range, calls ExecuteEvents with bMissile=0, performs additional melee events/durability/thorns work, calls FinalizeDamage and unlinks/frees the node. Its breadth makes it unsafe as a blind splash-target primitive.

entries.name: D2GAME_EnumerateUnitsInArea
entries.notes: Confirmed-static area-enumeration core with logical bounds 0x4398B0..0x439C04, unique 18-byte signature and eight direct callers. Its ten-position ABI carries game, origin, room/x/y descriptor, radius, mask, callback, user context, a special monster filter and source provenance. It walks the supplied room array and each room unit list in native order, applies square and inclusive radius gates and invokes callback(ctx,candidate). MEC-W07 remains partial because the upstream room-list membership and uniqueness/dedup invariants are not yet proven.

entries.name: DUNGEON_GetRoomListAndCount
entries.notes: Confirmed-static room-list accessor with bounds 0x2EFDE0..0x2EFDED, unique 13-byte body and ABI (room, roomListOut, roomCountOut) -> void. It returns room+0 and the count at room+0x40. Its use by the area enumerator is proven, but the exact adjacent-room membership is not promoted until the native writer/builder is identified.

entries.name: DUNGEON_GetFirstUnitInRoom
entries.notes: Confirmed-static one-argument room-unit-list accessor with bounds 0x2EFD90..0x2EFD98 and unique 8-byte body. It returns the pointer at room+0xA8 and is used by the governed area-enumeration traversal.

entries.name: UNITS_GetNextUnitInRoom
entries.notes: Confirmed-static room-list next-unit accessor with logical bounds 0x34B4A0..0x34B4DB and a unique strict 46-byte signature. It returns unit+0x160; the area enumerator reads this next pointer before filters and callback invocation.

entries.name: DUNGEON_DoesRoomIntersectSearchSquare
entries.notes: Confirmed-static inclusive broad-phase test with bounds 0x3256E0..0x325760 and unique 30-byte signature. ABI (room, centerX, centerY, radius) -> bool compares the search square against the room rectangle before per-unit traversal.

entries.name: COORDS_GetSquaredDistance
entries.notes: Confirmed-static squared-distance helper with bounds 0x3412C0..0x3412D3 and unique 19-byte body. ABI (x1, y1, x2, y2) -> int32 computes (x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2; the area enumerator accepts candidates when this value is less than or equal to radius squared.

entries.name: D2GAME_EventFunc7_Knockback
entries.notes: Confirmed-static EventFunc7 Knockback handler with logical bounds 0x583E00..0x583F0F, a unique 30-byte entry signature and the governed nine-position event callback ABI. It has zero direct xrefs because the 92777 event-list dispatcher invokes callbacks indirectly. MeleeSplash filters this handler only while its thread-local synthetic-secondary guard is active.

entries.name: D2GAME_EventFunc9_Blind
entries.notes: Confirmed-static EventFunc9 Blind handler with logical bounds 0x583400..0x58357B, a unique 30-byte entry signature and the governed nine-position event callback ABI. It has zero direct xrefs because dispatch is indirect. MeleeSplash filters it only for synthetic secondary resolution.

entries.name: D2GAME_EventFunc19_Slow
entries.notes: Confirmed-static EventFunc19 Slow handler with logical bounds 0x5849D0..0x584B56, a unique 33-byte entry signature and the governed nine-position event callback ABI. It has zero direct xrefs because dispatch is indirect. MeleeSplash filters it only for synthetic secondary resolution.

entries.name: D2GAME_EventFunc21_SkillOnGetHit
entries.notes: Confirmed-static EventFunc21 SkillOnGetHit handler with logical bounds 0x5837F0..0x583995, a unique 31-byte entry signature and the governed nine-position event callback ABI. It has zero direct xrefs because dispatch is indirect. MeleeSplash filters it only for synthetic secondary resolution.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_PreCriticalApplyDamageBonusesCall
entries.notes: Confirmed-static call inside SUNITDMG_FillDamageValues to 0x44D710 ApplyDamageBonuses. The five bytes E8 5F 14 00 00 and unique 21-byte context are governed. Its continuation at 0x44C2B1 stores EAX to D2Damage+0x18 immediately before the native mode-gated Critical/Deadly sequence.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_PreEvent3ApplyDamageEventCall
entries.notes: Confirmed-static conditional Event 3 call inside SUNITDMG_FillDamageValues. The five bytes E8 CD 09 00 00 and unique 34-byte context from 0x44CB89 are governed. ABI is int32(game, event, defender, attacker, D2Damage*), with continuation 0x44CBA3.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_DirectMeleeFillDamageValuesCall
entries.notes: Confirmed-static direct melee call to SUNITDMG_FillDamageValues with continuation 0x4300BB. Its unique 29-byte context begins at 0x43009E. The same stack D2Damage at caller rsp+0x70 then passes through 0x56CBE0 and into SUNITDMG_PrepareAndQueueCombatRecord at 0x4300DE with hit flag 0x02, so the wrapper skips a second Fill and continues through canonical Calculate, Allocate and Consume. A 2026-08-09 runtime witness with normal Attack confirmed capture at return 0x4300BB and a three-target synthetic burst.

entries.name: SEED_RollPowerOfTwo
entries.notes: Exact 35-byte leaf routine advancing the supplied native seed and returning nextLow & (upperBound - 1). The Rare generator calls it at 0x58BC98 with upperBound 8. ProgressiveAffixesPlugin validates it and uses it only for semantic vanilla fallback.

entries.name: D2GAME_ITEMS_GenerateCraftedAffixes
entries.notes: Build-92777 Crafted affix generator with observed ABI (item, generation) -> int32. The governed block reads item level at generation+0x18, computes minima at ilvl 1/31/51/71, rolls 0..4 through 0x153B00, then applies the selected count through native prefix/suffix selection and finalization.

entries.name: CraftedAffixCountRollCall
entries.notes: Exact five-byte call E8 E0 98 BC FF to SEED_RollLimitedRandomNumber inside the Crafted generator. ProgressiveAffixesPlugin redirects it through a near relay receiving the existing seed in RCX, item in R15 and generation in R12.

entries.name: CraftedAffixVanillaMinimumClamp
entries.notes: Five-byte CMP/CMOVA sequence 3B D8 0F 47 C3 that clamps the Crafted RNG result to the vanilla ilvl minimum. ProgressiveAffixesPlugin NOPs it only after its relay has selected the complete configured 1..4 count.

entries.name: D2GAME_ITEMS_GenerateRareAffixes
entries.notes: Build-92777 Rare affix generator with observed ABI (item, generation) -> int32. It resolves existing affix state, obtains the native item seed, selects a 3..4 jewel count or regular eight-entry count, then uses native prefix/suffix selection with three-per-side limits and finalization.

entries.name: RareJewelAffixCountBranch
entries.notes: Two-byte JNE +0x29 separating the native jewel 3..4 LCG path from the regular Rare table path. ProgressiveAffixesPlugin changes it to JMP so jewels and regular items reach one configured selector while still consuming exactly one seed step.

entries.name: RareAffixCountSelectionBlock
entries.notes: Exact 30-byte block 0x58BC90..0x58BCAD loading bound 8, rolling the item seed and mapping the index through the native count table. ProgressiveAffixesPlugin replaces the full block with a rel32 call, moves EAX to R12D, restores R9=seed and rejoins the untouched loop at 0x58BCAE.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_WeaponMasteryCriticalChanceCall
entries.notes: Exact five-byte call E8 18 12 EF FF inside SUNITDMG_FillDamageValues to the weapon-mastery Critical chance helper. The governed context supplies attacker, active weapon, argument3=0 and argument4=2; BKVCombat preserves that callee ABI and caps only the returned chance when its Critical policy is operational.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_PassiveCriticalChanceCall
entries.notes: Exact five-byte call E8 F0 8C EA FF inside SUNITDMG_FillDamageValues to STATLIST_GetUnitStat for passive_critical_strike stat 337, layer 0. It is reached only after the weapon-mastery Critical branch fails and retains the native (unit, statId, layer) -> int32 ABI.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_DeadlyStrikeChanceCall
entries.notes: Exact five-byte call E8 DC 98 EA FF inside SUNITDMG_FillDamageValues to STATLIST_UnitGetStatValue for item_deadlystrike stat 141, layer 0. It is reached only after both Critical branches fail and retains the native layered-stat ABI.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_DeadlyStrikeSuccessTail
entries.notes: Exact 17-byte native success tail 8B 47 18 03 C0 89 47 18 B8 00 20 00 00 66 09 47 04. The unique branch context at 0x44C3C2 distinguishes the Deadly-success path from Critical success; BKVCombat redirects this block and rejoins at 0x44C3D9 so only Deadly uses the configured 1.5x multiplier.

entries.name: D2GAME_EventFunc16_CrushingBlowCoreCall
entries.notes: Exact five-byte call E8 74 E9 FF FF from EventFunc16 to D2GAME_ApplyCrushingBlowCore at 0x581BD0. The preserved x64 ABI is int32(game, attacker, target, context); the int32 return is authoritative and EventFunc16 itself remains owned by MeleeSplash in the supported stack.

entries.name: D2GAME_EventFunc15_OpenWoundsStatListCall
entries.notes: Exact five-byte call E8 28 FA EA FF from EventFunc15 to D2GAME_ApplyCurseStateStatList at 0x433D20. ABI is StatList* (ApplyArgs*), where the 0x30-byte argument record carries source, target, skill, duration, stat, state and optional removal callback; EventFunc15 itself remains owned by MeleeSplash.

entries.name: D2GAME_EventFunc05_LifeTap
entries.notes: Confirmed-static Life Tap handler with logical bounds 0x55BCD0..0x55BFAC and a validated 32-byte entry signature. It uses the native event-callback frame and derives a separate life credit from resolved physical damage; it is not ordinary stat-60 life steal and BKVCombat validates but never hooks it.

entries.name: D2GAME_GetMinionOwner
entries.notes: Confirmed-static monster-minion owner resolver with logical bounds 0x4A53C0..0x4A547C, validated 32-byte entry signature and ABI Unit* (Unit* monster). It validates unit type, reads the monster owner identity and re-resolves that owner through SUNIT_GetServerUnit; null is returned when no live owner is available.

entries.name: UNITS_GetGame
entries.notes: Confirmed-static unit-to-game accessor with logical bounds 0x48FF00..0x48FF3A, validated 32-byte entry signature and ABI Game* (Unit*). For a valid unit it returns the pointer at unit+0xD8; BKVCombat uses it transiently while creating server-owned Open Wounds stat lists. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints the same entry and obtains the authoritative game from the attacker, or the defender when no attacker exists, before native Fire resolution.

entries.name: STATLIST_GetStatListFromUnitAndState
entries.notes: Confirmed-static state-list lookup with validated entry signature and ABI StatList* (Unit*, int32 state). The Open Wounds lifecycle uses it to detect state 62 before disabling that state in the custom removal callback.

entries.name: STATLIST_AllocStatList
entries.notes: Confirmed-static stat-list allocator with validated 32-byte entry signature and ABI StatList* (uint32 flags, int32 expireFrame, int32 sourceType, uint32 sourceGuid). BKVCombat uses only the governed Open Wounds flags and immediately frees any partially initialized list on validation failure.

entries.name: STATLIST_SetStatListState
entries.notes: Exact nine-byte leaf setter 48 85 C9 74 03 89 51 20 C3 with ABI void (StatList*, int32 state). It stores the state at StatList+0x20 and is null-safe.

entries.name: STATLIST_SetStatListSkillId
entries.notes: Confirmed-static stat-list skill-ID setter with bounds 0x2F79B0..0x2F79F2, validated 32-byte signature and ABI void (StatList*, int32 skillId). It stores the value at StatList+0x28.

entries.name: STATLIST_SetStatListSkillLevel
entries.notes: Confirmed-static stat-list skill-level setter with bounds 0x2F7A00..0x2F7A42, validated 32-byte signature and ABI void (StatList*, int32 skillLevel). It stores the value at StatList+0x2C.

entries.name: STATLIST_SetStatListStat
entries.notes: Confirmed-static stat-list stat setter with bounds 0x2F7C00..0x2F7C14, validated 21-byte signature and ABI void (uint8 dataContext, StatList*, int32 statId, int32 value, uint16 layer). It tail-calls the native stat insertion primitive and is used for the negative stat-74 Open Wounds rate.

entries.name: STATLIST_SetStatListRemoveCallback
entries.notes: Exact 13-byte leaf setter 48 85 C9 74 07 48 89 91 80 00 00 00 C3 with ABI void (StatList*, RemoveCallback). It stores the callback at StatList+0x80 and is null-safe.

entries.name: STATLIST_SetStatListExpireFrame
entries.notes: Exact expire-frame setter with bounds 0x2F7AB0..0x2F7AC9 and validated 26-byte signature. ABI is void (StatList*, int32 frame); a positive frame sets list flag 0x2 and stores the frame as float at StatList+0x24.

entries.name: STATLIST_PostStatList
entries.notes: Confirmed-static stat-list posting primitive with validated 32-byte entry signature and ABI void (Unit* target, StatList*, int32 update). It links the list under the target's extended stat-list owner and updates the unit aggregate.

entries.name: STATLIST_UnlinkStatList
entries.notes: Confirmed-static unlink wrapper with bounds 0x2F7920..0x2F7939, validated 26-byte signature and ABI void (Unit* target, StatList*). It derives the target data context before tail-calling the internal unlink primitive.

entries.name: STATLIST_FreeStatList
entries.notes: Exact 16-byte stat-list free wrapper with bounds 0x2F4180..0x2F418F and ABI void (uint8 dataContext, StatList*). BKVCombat calls it only for a newly allocated unposted list or after explicit unlink, providing fail-closed rollback after allocation or post-validation failure.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_ApplyLifeAndManaLeechCall
entries.notes: Exact five-byte call E8 53 3C 00 00 from SUNITDMG_ExecuteEvents to the unique leech consumer at 0x450C90. The governed context starts at 0x44D02C and preserves ABI void (game, attacker, defender, D2Damage*); BKVCombat validates this baseline but installs no leech hook.

entries.name: SOUNDENVIRON_GetRecord
entries.notes: Receives the sound-environment index in ECX, resolves data context 3, reads the compiled row count at DataTables+0x508 and returns the indexed record only when 0 <= index < count. An index equal to the count reaches the native assertion at 0x3B0C82. This proves that deleting stable row 75 while the Terror Zone resolver can still request index 75 is invalid.

entries.name: InheritedSoundEnvironmentSongStore
entries.notes: Unique six-byte store 89 05 1F B5 88 02 in build 92777. It copies only the inherited sound-environment Song field loaded from record+0x34 into the active environment. NOPing this store preserves the base area's current music while leaving the ten adjacent inherited ambience and event assignments native.

entries.name: MONSTERUNIQUE_UMod30_AuraEnchanted
entries.notes: Exact build-92777 Aura Enchanted callback reached through index 30 of the 43-entry MonUMod dispatcher at RVA 0x2395FE0. Its unique 32-byte entry signature is 40 55 53 57 48 8B EC 48 83 EC 70 41 8B D8 48 8B F9 48 85 C9 74 0A E8 E5 5C EB FF 83 F8 01 74 1B. entries.name: CLIENT_GetUnitByIdAndType
entries.notes: Resolves a client unit with ABI (unitId in ECX, unitType in EDX) -> Unit*. The native caller at 0x198D66 loads the packet type byte and unit id before calling it. Its entry proves the client hash-table base at 0x2A23910, 128 buckets per unit type through mask 0x7F, and a 0x400-byte type stride. Its strict build-92777 signature is unique and differs from the adjacent server-unit lookup at 0x9A5A0 by its backing table and tail displacement. Floating Damage 1.2.8 resolves one requested monster at a native frame rendezvous; MapSense 0.12.0 fingerprints the same table contract before bounded read-only monster-bucket enumeration. Neither plugin retains returned Unit pointers.

entries.name: CLIENT_UpdateCameraOffsets
entries.notes: Updates gameplay camera offsets from the local player. It resolves CLIENT_GetLocalDataContext and CLIENT_GetLocalPlayer, reads the player's client coordinates, subtracts half the native viewport dimensions and applies the optional camera displacement. Its only direct call is 0x93D79 in the main client-frame pass. The strict 33-byte build-92777 entry signature is unique. Floating Damage 1.2.8 invokes the original first, then uses this frame rendezvous to service every active target request with current camera state; gameplay confirmation remains required.

entries.name: RENDER_GetThreadContextRoot
entries.notes: Returns the renderer thread-context root, lazily initialized through TLS. Native unit-label projection callers read the active render context at +0x20 before calling RENDER_ProjectUnitToScreen. The strict 37-byte build-92777 entry signature is unique.

entries.name: RENDER_ProjectUnitToScreen
entries.notes: Projects a Unit into native UI float coordinates with observed ABI (renderContext, Unit*, floatXYOut, useUnitHeight bool) -> bool. Six direct callers establish the same first three arguments; 0x198F75 passes R9B=1, tests AL, converts the two output floats and bounds them with UI_GetNativeWidth/Height. The strict 61-byte build-92777 entry signature is unique. Runtime invalidated calling it from Floating Damage 1.2.5's overlay thread because its render context is TLS-bound. Gameplay then invalidated 1.2.6's passive observation and 1.2.7's conditional-entry rendezvous: moving the camera left only the principal target refreshed. Floating Damage 1.2.8 no longer hooks this entry; it calls the verified function from the native camera-frame rendezvous after CLIENT_UpdateCameraOffsets.

entries.name: SUNITDMG_MainHitpointsCommitCall
entries.notes: Exact five-byte call E8 78 AC EA FF from SUNITDMG_ExecuteEvents to STATLIST_SetUnitStat for the main target HP mutation. The unique 21-byte context begins at 0x44D083 and passes defender, stat 6, the post-damage fixed-point HP and layer 0; R14 and RDI still hold attacker and D2Damage. entries.name: D2GAME_SKILLS_ServerDoHandler
entries.notes: Authoritative server skill do-handler with observed x64 ABI int32 (game, unit, skillId, skillLevel, consumeResources, itemCast, itemEffect). Eight direct callers prove manual executions use consumeResources=1,itemCast=0,itemEffect=0, while native item CTC uses itemCast=1. The function resolves the context-aware SkillsTxt row, executes its SrvDo handler and returns nonzero only on success. Cast Triggers wraps the unique strict 32-byte entry and dispatches doactive only after a successful manual player cast; D2MOO is semantic evidence only.

entries.name: D2GAME_ApplyUnitStatEvent
entries.notes: Safe wrapper with observed ABI int32 (game, eventId, sourceUnit, targetUnit, damage). It constructs the native event context, accepts a null damage pointer and calls D2GAME_DispatchUnitStatEventList at 0x5881E0. Cast Triggers invokes it with event 4 doactive after a successful eligible cast. Its strict 18-byte entry signature is unique in the governed corpus reused for current D2R 3.3.93847.

entries.name: DATATBLS_GetSkillsTxtRecordForContext
entries.notes: Context-aware SkillsTxt lookup with observed ABI (uint8 dataContext, int32 skillId) -> compiled record pointer. It resolves the per-context table at +0x11B0/+0x11B8 and multiplies the validated row index by the proven 0x2EC record stride at 0x9780B. Cast Triggers reads the flags QWORD at +0x24, player animation at +0x30 and sequence transition at +0x32. Its strict 40-byte entry signature is unique. ArmageddonCtCFix uses the same ABI for its two supported skills and fingerprints this entry before installing any hook.

entries.name: SKILLITEM_CastOnTarget
entries.notes: Native item-skill caster for a unit target with observed ABI int32 (caster, skillId, skillLevel, target, flag). EventFunc20 calls it at 0x583C7F and 0x583CB4 after its native chance roll and target-policy selection. Cast Triggers wraps the unique strict 45-byte entry, substitutes only its internal level-zero marker, and suspends the dispatch context while the triggered skill runs so nested procs cannot inherit the source level. The PluginPack Whirlwind CTC patch is later in the original body at 0x589736 and does not overlap this entry ownership.

entries.name: SKILLITEM_CastAtPosition
entries.notes: Native item-skill position caster with observed ABI int32 (caster, skillId, skillLevel, x, y, flag). EventFunc20 calls it at 0x583CE1 when no unit target is selected. Cast Triggers wraps the unique strict 43-byte entry and applies the same bounded level-zero substitution and recursion suspension as the target path. The PluginPack state patch at 0x58986B is inside the original body and does not overlap entry ownership.

entries.name: SUNIT_GetTargetUnit
entries.notes: Resolves the current server target with observed ABI (game, sourceUnit) -> targetUnit. Cast Triggers uses it after a successful source cast so EventFunc20 retains native unit-target behavior. Its strict 30-byte entry signature is unique in the governed corpus.

entries.name: UNITS_GetUnitType
entries.notes: Returns Unit+0x00 for a non-null Unit and the native invalid unit type 6 for null. Cast Triggers requires type 0 player before dispatching doactive. Its strict 32-byte entry signature is unique in the governed corpus.

entries.name: D2GAME_PACKETCALLBACK_Rcv0x3B_AllocateSkillPoints
entries.notes: Authoritative server callback with observed ABI (game, player, packet, packetSize) -> int32. A controlled D2R 3.3.93847 runtime read proved slot 0x3B of the server callback table at D2R+0x1D2A790 points here. It requires exactly five bytes, decodes the skill id at +1 and additional-rank marker at +3, validates the id against the compiled SkillsTxt count, resolves the skill and its MaxLvl, reads the current base rank, then applies ranks through the native server mutation helper at 0x438670 until the request is exhausted or a validation/cap/mutation fails. The callback never reads SkillPage, SkillRow or SkillColumn, so authoritative allocation is independent of the UI page number.

entries.name: ResistanceFloorUncappedClampImmediate

entries.name: UI_CalculateIncomingHitChance
entries.notes: Character Screen defensive hit-chance calculator. Its single direct caller at 0x14E8242 retains the EAX result in EBX and passes it as ECX to UI_FormatIncomingHitChanceTooltip at 0x14E8262. The function computes the raw monster-versus-player chance and returns without a terminal 5%-95% clamp; the remaining vanilla clamp is owned by the formatter.

entries.name: UI_FormatIncomingHitChanceTooltip

It clamps the incoming value in the unique 18-byte sequence at 0x1514CBD, then formats localization id 10104 charmontohit1X or 10105 charmontohit2X. This is the post-calculation clamp omitted by the original seven-write Hit Chance Bounds patch.

entries.notes: Four-byte immediate 5F 00 00 00 in MOV EAX,95 at 0x1514CC9 inside UI_FormatIncomingHitChanceTooltip. It shares the unique governed clamp sequence beginning at 0x1514CBD. entries.name: DATATBLS_GetDifficultyRecord
entries.notes: Returns the native difficulty record with observed Windows x64 ABI (dataSet, difficulty) -> pointer. The unique 38-byte witness at 0x44DF40 proves the call order and the source bytes at Game+0x106 and Game+0x104. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints the resolver's unique 32-byte entry before constructing its synthetic Fire-resolution context.

entries.name: DATATBLS_CompileStatesTxt_OverlayFieldWitness
entries.notes: Unique 33-byte read-only field-descriptor witness inside the StatesTxt compiler. It assigns TXT field type 0x16 to record offset +0x02, then begins the same descriptor for +0x04. Together with the subsequent +0x06/+0x08 descriptors, this proves that the first compiled state overlay is the 16-bit word at record+0x02.

entries.notes: Unique 22-byte instruction-aligned read-only prefix in the StatesTxt loader. It passes record size 0x44 to the governed table compiler before installing the resulting vector. The immediately following CALL is deliberately excluded because D2RLoader may redirect that compiler integration surface before plugins load; its target is irrelevant to the stride proof. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints only this stable prefix before calculating state 115 as base + 115*0x44.

entries.name: DATATBLS_CompileStatesTxt_VectorLayoutWitness
entries.notes: Unique 26-byte read-only witness in the StatesTxt loader. It takes the destination vector at DataTables+0x290 and transfers the newly compiled state records into it. The associated state count is independently witnessed at DataTables+0x298 by STATES_ToggleState.

entries.name: UNITS_SetOverlay
entries.notes: Applies a direct overlay to a unit with observed Windows x64 ABI void (unit, overlayId, unusedLayer). The entry validates the overlay index, obtains or allocates a stat list with internal flag 0x80, writes the overlay ID to unit_dooverlay stat 178 and refreshes the unit. Its strict unique 24-byte entry signature is 48 89 5C 24 18 55 57 41 56 48 83 EC 30 45 8B F0 8B FA 48 8B D9 48 85 C9. BKVCombat borrows it for Crushing Blow. Burn Damage Fix 2.1 also borrows it without hooking and applies fire_hit overlay 81 on layer 0 immediately after a positive state-confirmed Burn application, then periodically while state burning 115 remains active and the unit is alive. The direct-overlay channel is last-write-wins; Burn Damage Fix counts a foreign prior value before replacing it. Direct unit targeting does not guarantee that each emitted particle remains attached after spawning.

entries.name: UNITS_SetOverlay_UnitDoOverlayStatWitness
entries.notes: Unique read-only 30-byte witness 0F B6 8B BD 01 00 00 44 0F B7 CF 41 B8 B2 00 00 00 48 8B D6 44 89 74 24 20 E8 96 9E FA FF inside UNITS_SetOverlay. The MOV R8D,0xB2 proves that the overlay ID is written as unit_dooverlay stat 178; the separate 0x80 constant is a stat-list flag, not a stat ID. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints this witness before reading stat 178 for diagnostic arbitration.

entries.name: MONSTERS_GetHirelingTypeId
entries.notes: Returns zero for an ordinary monster and a nonzero hireling type for a hireling. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints its unique 24-byte entry and excludes hirelings from the monster-attacker/defender flags passed to the native Fire resolver. BKVCombat uses the same helper to distinguish hirelings in Crushing Blow and Open Wounds policy.

It calls GetItemDataContext, passes AL to GetDataTablesForContext, and loads the signed-safe state count from DataTables+0x298 before checking the requested id. Burn Damage Fix fingerprints this exact context/count contract before reading compiled state 115.

entries.name: StatesTxtRecord_EmptyOverlaySentinelWitness
entries.notes: Unique 47-byte initializer for records of stride 0x44. It zeroes the remaining record fields, writes dword 0xFFFF0000 at +0 and advances by 0x44; combined with the native StatesTxt field descriptor, this proves state id 0 at +0 and the empty first-overlay sentinel 0xFFFF at +2. Burn Damage Fix 2.2 uses only an atomic compare/exchange 224 -> 0xFFFF and therefore preserves custom overlay ids.

entries.name: SUNIT_IsDead

It reports dead for a null or death-flagged unit, for player death/dead modes 0/17, for monster death/dead modes 0/12 and conservatively for unsupported unit types. It validates unit type 1, bounds eventType to 0..14 and forwards callback arguments 4, 5 and 6 to the selected handler; event type 3 selects monster stat regeneration at 0x448C00. entries.notes: Unique 38-byte read-only witness 48 89 4C 24 30 0F B6 91 04 01 00 00 48 8B F9 48 89 4C 24 40 4D 8B F9 0F B6 89 06 01 00 00 49 8B F0 E8 CA 28 EB FF. entries.name: SKILLITEM_HandleItemEffectSkill
entries.notes: Authoritative server item-effect helper with observed ABI (game, unit, skillId, skillLevel, target, x, y, unitTypeOut, unitGuidOut, xOut, yOut, flag) -> int32. It resolves the context SkillsTxt record and refuses a zero ItemEffect word at record+0x20A before entering native target selection and the central skill handler. It saves the current target unit and first-point coordinates, temporarily installs the passed unit or position, applies SkillsTxt ItemTarget semantics, executes the central handler, then restores the saved descriptor. Its entry and semantics are byte-identical in the governed common corpus for 92777 and 93847. ArmageddonCtCFix owns this entry only for a thread-local item cast of configured skill IDs 249 and 250.

entries.name: SKILLS_SrvDo124_Armageddon_Hurricane
entries.notes: Shared authoritative start callback for Armageddon and Hurricane with ABI (game, unit, skillId, skillLevel) -> int32. It requires UNITS_GetUsedSkill to identify the requested skill, creates or refreshes the aura state and active event, then stores a random periodic seed at D2Skill+0x24. A native chance-to-cast call has no matching used skill, which is the second proven failure gate after ItemEffect.

entries.name: SKILLS_SrvDo146_ArmageddonActive
entries.notes: Armageddon active-state callback with ABI (game, unit, skillId, skillLevel) -> int32. After validating the state it resolves the highest matching skill through 0x33DD40, consumes the seed at D2Skill+0x24, updates that seed and schedules the next active event. ArmageddonCtCFix temporarily links a stack-local surrogate only when its own synthetic CtC start retained a seed for the exact unit identity. Version 0.1.1 borrows the separately fingerprinted STATES_CheckState predicate at 0x3351B0 before this callback and after a zero return so natural expiration erases the retained seed without treating every native zero return as expiration.

entries.name: SKILLS_SrvDo145_HurricaneActive
entries.notes: Hurricane active-state callback with ABI (game, unit, skillId, skillLevel) -> int32. Unlike Armageddon's active callback it does not resolve or retain a D2Skill node after SrvDo124 has successfully established the state and event. ArmageddonCtCFix therefore does not hook this entry.

entries.name: SKILLS_GetHighestLevelSkillFromUnitAndId
entries.notes: Resolves the highest eligible D2Skill for a unit and skill ID with observed ABI (unit, skillId, selectionFlag) -> D2Skill*. The false-selection path scans SkillList+0x00, identifies each node through its SkillsTxt pointer at +0x00 and filters the node flag at +0x54. Armageddon's active callback calls it with selectionFlag false.

entries.name: PATH_GetRoom
entries.notes: Returns the ActiveRoom pointer stored at dynamic-path offset +0x20. UNITS_GetRoom tail-jumps here for player units; MapSense 0.9.3 validates this five-byte body as part of the current-level witness chain. The signature 48 8B 41 20 C3 is unique in the governed 92777 corpus reused for target 3.3.93847.

entries.name: ACTIVEROOM_GetDrlgRoom
entries.notes: Leaf accessor with ABI (ActiveRoom*) -> DrlgRoom*. Its complete body returns ActiveRoom+0x18 and is followed by an aligned trap padding run. MapSense 0.9.5 uses it instead of duplicating this native field access while resolving both the player's current level and linked RoomTile destinations. The strict 16-byte body-plus-padding witness is unique in the governed common corpus for targets 92777 and 93847.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_GetLevelId
entries.notes: Returns the levelId through DrlgRoom+0x90 (Level*) and Level+0x1F8. MapSense 0.9.3 uses the same proven field chain after UNITS_GetRoom and ActiveRoom+0x18 to invalidate stale navigation immediately on a level transition. Its complete 14-byte body is unique in the governed 92777 corpus shared with target 3.3.93847.

entries.name: DRLGWARP_ResolveRoomTileLink
entries.notes: ABI (uint8 dataContext, DrlgRoom* sourceRoom, int32 sourcePresetId, int32* outReciprocalPresetId, LvlWarpTxt** outReciprocalLvlWarpTxt) -> ActiveRoom*. Initializes the source room, matches sourcePresetId against RoomTile+0x20 (LvlWarpTxt*) +0x2C in the source RoomTile chain at +0x78, follows RoomTile+0x00 to the destination DrlgRoom, validates the reciprocal RoomTile, writes the reciprocal LvlWarp identifier and record pointer, initializes the destination room when needed, and returns its ActiveRoom; unresolved reciprocal links return null. The wrapper at 0x361070 converts the returned ActiveRoom through +0x18, DrlgRoom+0x90 and Level+0x1F8 into the destination LevelId. MapSense 0.9.4 called this resolver on the UI thread. Live 0.9.9 diagnostics proved that its reciprocal requirement rejects valid lazy source-side links in Tamoe Highland, Barracks, and Jail Level 1. MapSense 0.10.0 therefore materializes each source room and reads the already-valid destination DrlgRoom directly from RoomTile+0x00; the independent 15-byte witness at 0x3DA9FB proves RoomTile+0x00, destination DrlgRoom+0x78, and reciprocal RoomTile+0x00. The 27-byte entry signature 48 89 5C 24 08 48 89 74 24 10 48 89 7C 24 18 41 56 48 83 EC 20 4D 8B F1 41 8B F8 is unique in the governed common corpus.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_FindWaypointRoomAndCoordinates
entries.notes: ABI (uint8 dataContext, Level* level, int32* outTileX, int32* outTileY) -> DrlgRoom*. Iterates Level+0x10 rooms, selects a room whose +0x50 flags intersect 0x30000, initializes it, then scans PresetUnit type 2 objects whose ObjectsTxt SubClass byte at +0x127 carries 0x40. On an exact waypoint match it writes room tile coordinates plus preset-relative coordinates divided by five; native callers initialize both outputs to -1 and fall back to the room center if either remains unset. MapSense 0.9.4 accepts only an exact non-null result with valid outputs, converts game tiles to world subtiles, and publishes no room-center or first-preset fallback. The 18-byte entry signature 48 89 6C 24 18 57 41 56 41 57 48 83 EC 20 48 8B 7A 10 is unique in the governed common corpus.

entries.name: DRLG_GetLevel
entries.notes: Resolves a Level with ABI (uint8 dataContext, Drlg*, int32 levelId) -> Level*. It traverses Drlg+0x868 through Level+0x1B8 and compares Level+0x1F8, but allocates and links a new Level when the target is absent. Native consumers pair it with DRLG_InitLevel when Level+0x10 is null. Since MapSense 0.9.9, Reveal owns the fingerprinted helper used by Navigation to resolve levels inside the captured client DRLG. MapSense 0.10.0 initializes only the explicit progression target and configured custom targets present in the current Level's eight Vis slots before source RoomTile enumeration; unavailable targets remain pending and never produce guessed lines.

entries.name: DRLG_InitLevel
entries.notes: Initializes the room chain of a Level with ABI (uint8 dataContext, Level*) -> void. A native consumer at 0x3DD5E3 first checks Level+0x10. Since MapSense 0.9.9, Reveal owns the strictly fingerprinted call and invokes it only when Level+0x10 is null. MapSense 0.10.0 reuses that governed helper for the explicit progression target and configured custom targets present in the current Level's eight Vis slots before reading source RoomTile links.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_GetPresetUnits
entries.notes: Returns DrlgRoom+0x98 after checking room flag bits 18 and 26, and may set bit 26. MapSense avoids this mutation and reads +0x98 directly after proving that the current active Level already owns the room chain. The complete strict signature through the trailing return is unique.

entries.name: DRLGROOM_RebuildNearRoomVector
entries.notes: ABI (DrlgRoom*) -> void. Clears the vector size at DrlgRoom+0x18, iterates the owning Level+0x10 room chain through DrlgRoom+0x48, compares rectangle fields +0x60/+0x64/+0x68/+0x6C, appends qualifying room pointers through the vector at +0x10/+0x18/+0x20 and sorts them. MapSense 0.9.5 does not invoke this mutating routine because later DRLG linkage can add cross-level neighbours; it uses three strict interior witnesses from this function to prove the existing near-room vector layout before passively enumerating outdoor inter-level boundaries.

entries.name: CLIENT_FindUnitInTypeBucket
entries.notes: Client hash-chain lookup witness. It loads one bucket head, compares Unit+0x08 to the requested id and Unit+0x00 to the requested type, and advances through Unit+0x158 until a match or null. MapSense 0.12.0 fingerprints the complete 41-byte helper and uses only the proven +0x158 next-link layout for bounded read-only traversal of the monster table.

entries.name: CLIENT_UnitHashTable
entries.notes: Base of the client Unit hash table. Each unit type owns 128 pointer buckets (0x400 bytes), so monster type 1 begins at +0x400 and missile type 3 begins at +0xC00. MapSense 0.12.0 reads the monster buckets while the local-player automap pass is active; the missile-source foundation added on 2026-08-31 reads only the client type-3 buckets from the same rendezvous. Both paths follow the separately witnessed Unit+0x158 link, enforce per-bucket and total traversal caps and retain no native Unit pointer.

entries.name: UNITS_MissileTypeAndDataWitness

entries.name: ITEMS_SerializeItemComplete_BoundedStatIdWrite
entries.notes: Exact unique 50-byte governed site [0x37F174,0x37F1A6) covers the prerequisite nonzero rejection, unsafe 511-DWORD indexed comparison, 0x1FF clamp/default, 9-bit setup and writer CALL. ISC12 may mutate only [0x37F17C,0x37F1A1): retain native table comparison for IDs below 511, bypass it for 511..4094, then use 0xFFF and 12 bits. The CALL is never rewritten: runtime may use the native target directly or an exactly attested D2RCore WriteItemSaveStatId provider whose 1.1/1.2 body, PDATA, unwind and live slot all forward to D2R+0xA1B710. Publication requires every promoted owner, table, snapshot, direct-ID and low compound witness to match.

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemAction9CPreparationWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 31-byte sequence saves the current ItemData+0x18 flags and applies the 0x9C caller mask before the real serializer. Together with the restore calls after serialization, it proves that a scratch serialization at function entry is not byte-equivalent by construction.

entries.name: D2GAME_ItemAction9CBeforeQueueWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 139-byte prefix proves recursion R9D=0, serializer capacity 0xF4, header increment 8, diagnostic comparison 0xFC, item-state restoration and queue arguments for one 0x9C root node. It ends immediately before the mutable range [0x479E10,0x479E15); the safe native payload ceiling is 244 bytes.

entries.notes: Exact unique interior epilogue returns zero when the bit-writer overflow flag is set. Item-action producers still queue their 8/13-byte header after this return, so G9-A must reject the complete item tree before the first queue rather than relying on this late signal.

entries.name: CLIENT_ItemAction9CPayloadBoundWitness

entries.name: D2GAME_QueueServerPacketSpanDispatchWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 39-byte interior sequence builds packet+length and synchronously dispatches the [packet, packet+length] span through the client sink. This proves each source-prepared G9-A relay must copy producer stack packets before returning. A later flush through the untouched queue entry preserves packet order but delays queue-side effects and therefore still requires semantic, reentry and backpressure qualification.

entries.name: D2GAME_SocketedItemSeparate9DWalkerWitness
entries.notes: Exact unique 102-byte inventory-walk window calls INVENTORY_GetFirstItem, checks the result, sends it through D2GAME_SendItemAction9D at 0x481BFE, calls INVENTORY_GetNextItem and branches back to the same send path while one remains. Because each 0x9D producer captures its node then recursively invokes this walker before returning to the parent's GetNextItem, the native sequence is depth-first preorder. The G9-A source transaction now models this order, parent/item nesting and same-thread recursion, but runtime all-or-none proof remains blocked.
